request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now follow the new rule, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The only file I changed is `src/main/frontend/features/header/consolidated.slot.tsx`. The server, the stored data and the audit records needed no change, because the consolidated figures are worked out only in the front end.

- **Due-total and overdue-total:** the header now gathers every person's figure from every sheet in the tree. It leaves out n/a figures, then drops the single highest and single lowest across the whole tree when three or more people have a figure. It does this with the same trim function each sheet's own totals already use. Before, it added up each sheet's already-trimmed total.
- **People count:** names and aliases are compared the way the app already compares names (ignoring case and the spaces around them). People whose names or aliases match count as one person, including when the match is indirect: if A shares a name with B and B with C, all three count once. Retired people are still counted, as before.

The trim drops the highest and lowest single row on a sheet, not a merged person's total. The spec requires this. In its first scenario, the two "Ada" rows count once in the people count (5), but their figures stay separate for the trim. Trimming [1, 4, 4, 2, 3] gives the expected 9.00; adding the two Adas together first would give 7.00.

The per-grade totals and per-status counts work as they did before.
